title: Why rodent exclusion is important for your business
summary: Rats and mice in your business can mean bad news. Learn why proactive commercial rodent exclusion is important for your business and what that looks like.
body_markdown:
Rodent exclusion


is a preventive treatment that keeps rats and mice out of your business by physically sealing up cracks, gaps, and holes around your building. By blocking these entry points with durable materials, you can stop an infestation before it ever starts.


Rodents like[mice](https://www.rentokil.com/us/pest-control/mouse-control)


and[rats](https://www.rentokil.com/us/pest-control/rat-control)


can cause major headaches for a business by chewing through wires, contaminating products, and damaging your building's structure. By implementing[pest exclusion](https://www.rentokil.com/us/about/blog/all-industries/pest-proofing-your-business)


, you can help keep rodents out and your business running smoothly.


## The costs of a rodent infestation


Rodents need to chew constantly to wear down their fast-growing teeth. They can chew through electrical wiring, wooden support beams, insulation, and drywall. A chewed wire can easily start an electrical fire or shut down key machinery, causing unexpected downtime. Different[industries](https://www.rentokil.com/us/business-sectors)


face unique risks from rodent damage, with some of the most common including:


- **Bars and restaurants:**


Contaminated ingredients, ruined dry goods, and health department shutdowns.


- **Retail stores:**


Damaged apparel, chewed packaging, and lost foot traffic.


- **Warehouses and logistics:**


Chewed pallet goods, ruined shipping containers, and disrupted supply chains.


- **Office buildings:**


Damaged server cables, ruined insulation, and unpleasant odors that drive away clients.


Preventing these hazards requires comprehensive[commercial rodent control services](https://www.rentokil.com/us/pest-control/rodents)


that can address the root cause of entry.


## Understanding rodent exclusion vs. rodent control


Rodent exclusion


and rodent control work together, but they tackle the pest problem at very different times.


- **Exclusion is a proactive approach.**


Vulnerable areas around your facility are identified and sealed with rodent-proof materials to help prevent rats and mice from entering.


- **Traditional rodent control is reactive.**


Traps, bait stations, and other rodent control methods may be used to manage rodents that have already entered.


Keeping pests out is much easier than chasing them down later, which is why


commercial rodent exclusion


serves as the groundwork for


[integrated pest management (IPM)](https://www.rentokil.com/us/pest-control/integrated-pest-management)


. IPM prioritizes prevention first, which helps protect your building and minimizes the need for reactive treatments down the road.


## What rodent exclusion can look like at your business


To help keep pests out permanently, exclusion targets the structural gaps that rodents use to invade your commercial building. Since mice can fit through holes the size of a dime and rats only need a quarter-sized opening, our experts focus on blocking key structural access points across your facility, like:


- **Dock areas & overhead doors:**


Placing heavy-duty door seals to eliminate gaps under garage and loading doors.


- **Exterior shell & mortar:**


Reinforcing hairline cracks, weep holes, and foundation gaps using durable metal alloys.


- **Roof gaps & vents:**


Blocking access across upper levels, overhangs, and exhaust vents to stop climbing pests.


- **Plumbing & wire pass-throughs:**


Sealing pipe penetrations and electrical conduit gaps throughout interior and exterior walls.


## What materials can be used for


rodent exclusion


?


Not every material can withstand a determined rat or mouse. Rodents can gnaw through common materials such as foam, plastic, rubber, and wood, so lasting exclusion often requires stronger options. Depending on the entry point, metal mesh, sheet metal, concrete, reinforced door sweeps, and other rodent-resistant materials can be used to seal gaps and help prevent access.


At Rentokil, we take this protection a step further with our exclusive range of[Flexi Armour](https://www.rentokil.com/us/pest-control/exclusion)


TM


products. Made from tough, knitted stainless-steel wire, Flexi Armour creates a durable barrier that can be fitted to different gaps and openings around commercial facilities.


## The benefits of investing in


rodent exclusion


Spending money on exclusion now saves your business from major headaches later.[Commercial pest control](https://www.rentokil.com/us/pest-control)


that focuses on prevention offers clear advantages across every industry. Here is why sealing your building is a smart investment:


- **Long-term ROI:**


Preventing entry can help reduce repeated pest treatments, product loss, repairs, and facility maintenance costs. Keeping rats away from a[warehouse's](https://www.rentokil.com/us/business-sectors/warehousing-and-logistics)


electrical wiring can help save thousands of dollars in sudden repair bills.


- **Audit readiness:**


Proactive rodent prevention can help regulated businesses stay prepared for inspections and audits by the FDA, USDA, OSHA, and other applicable agencies.[Food manufacturing plants](https://www.rentokil.com/us/business-sectors/food-processing)


and[commercial kitchens](https://www.rentokil.com/us/business-sectors/bars-restaurants)


can maintain compliance without last-minute panics.


- **Brand protection:**


A single[rodent in a retail space](https://www.rentokil.com/us/about/blog/retail/rodents-in-retail-spaces)


can instantly drive away loyal shoppers. Keeping rodents out helps protect your online reviews, preserve customer trust, and prevent a public relations disaster.


## How to get started with


rodent exclusion


Rodent exclusion


starts with a thorough assessment of your facility. A[Rentokil](https://www.rentokil.com/us/) expert will look for potential entry points, signs of rodent activity, and other areas that could leave your building vulnerable. Based on what they find, they can recommend appropriate exclusion measures, such as sealing gaps or securing openings around doors and utilities with Flexi Armour or other rodent-proofing materials.


Exclusion can then work alongside ongoing monitoring and commercial pest control to provide complete protection for your facility.
